The average LSAT score for successful applicants is significantly higher, suggesting that this score may not adequately reflect the skills needed to pass the bar exam.

Second, your performance in your third year of studies placed you in the lowest decile compared to your peers, who generally performed much better. This indicates that your academic performance may not have met the expectations of law school admissions committees, which often correlate strong academic records with success on the bar exam.

Lastly, your first-year grades also placed you in the lowest decile, further reinforcing concerns about your academic preparedness. 

Given these factors, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your LSAT score and enhancing your academic performance in future studies.
